why: Where a committed Unit's outcome lives in the object store, and what a resuming attempt will accept as one.
note: THE HEARTBEAT SAYS WHICH UNITS FINISHED; THIS SAYS WHAT THEY PRODUCED. A checkpoint
(checkpoint.json) is a range set because a heartbeat is small, and a range set cannot carry a
Unit's output refs. So each Unit's outcome is written as ONE object, synchronously, BEFORE the
beat that reports it, and the checkpoint's `manifest_ref` names the batch's prefix. A retry
folds the finished Units back from these objects instead of re-running them (ADR 0060).
`commits/` IS ITS OWN TOP-LEVEL PREFIX, NOT A CORNER OF `units/`. Everything under
`units/run=<id>/` that ends in `.json` is counted as a ROW by the live row tail (rowTail.ts) and
read as one by a DuckDB glob over the run. A commit object is not a row, and putting it there
would inflate every run's count by its Unit count.
`run=` LEADS for the same measured reason it leads in blobkey.json: an object store prunes a LIST
only by literal prefix, and every reader of this tree (a retention sweep, an operator) asks by run.
A DECODE THAT REFUSES IS LOUD, NOT A RE-RUN. A body that names another batch or another Unit at
this key, or a version this reader does not know, is corruption or skew, and the engine fails the
attempt rather than guess. Reading it as 'not finished' would re-run silently; reading it as
'finished' with what it says would fold another Unit's output into this one.

keys.why: empty fields must still make a valid key — a missing segment is a path no reader can match
n10 must not prefix-collide n1 (the padding blobkey.json pins, reused)
a per-dispatch node id (catalog.py mints `{actor}-{uuid8}`) is not numeric and is kept
path and glob injection is neutered in EVERY segment, the batch id included
a chunked numeric shard keeps its padding
an index past five digits WIDENS rather than truncates: two Units must never share a key

encode.why: a committed Unit carries its output refs and nothing else
a Unit that pushed nothing commits an EMPTY list, not null — a reader refuses null
an isolated Unit carries its error and category, and `out` is still a list

decode.why: a committed Unit folds back as its output
a committed Unit that pushed nothing is FINISHED, and is not the same fact as a missing commit
an isolated Unit folds back as the same failure, so a retry reports it rather than re-poisoning the scope
an isolated Unit with no category reads as `exhausted`, the category the framework isolates by when nothing else is said
ANOTHER BATCH'S BODY AT THIS KEY IS REFUSED. The key carries the batch id, so a mismatch is corruption — and folding it would put another batch's output in this one
ANOTHER UNIT'S BODY AT THIS KEY IS REFUSED, for the same reason one level down
a body that does not say which Unit it is is not evidence about Unit 0
a body that does not say which batch it is is not evidence about this one
A FUTURE VERSION IS REFUSED, NOT PARTLY READ — the checkpoint's rule, for the same reason
an absent version is an encoder that did not say, which is the same risk
a committed body with no `out` is refused: folding it as empty would silently drop the Unit's rows
`out: null` is refused for the same reason — null is not an empty list
an error that is not an object cannot be reported as one
a body that is not an object at all is refused
